etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: First attested in 1586; either borrowed from Middle French desparat or directly from Latin disparātus, perfect passive participle of disparō (“to divide”) (see -ate (adjective-forming suffix) and -ate (noun-forming suffix)), from dis- (“apart”) + parō (“to arrange”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *dwóh₁ (“two”) and the root *per- (“carry forth”).
senses: Composed of inherently different or distinct elements; incongruous.
Essentially different; of different species, unlike but not opposed in pairs.
(chiefly in the plural) Any of a group of unequal or dissimilar things.
